blocks.text: Use It or Lose It: Make the Most of Your FSA Vision Benefits Before Year-End
blocks.html: Use It or Lose It: Make the Most of Your FSA Vision Benefits Before Year-End

If you’ve been contributing to a Flexible Spending Account (FSA) this year, here’s a friendly reminder to use it before it’s gone come year-end. Your FSA funds don’t carry over indefinitely, and December 31 is often the cutoff. That means any money you haven’t spent could vanish — unused. Why let a benefit slip through your fingers, especially when it can cover things you already need — like an FSA eye exam, new glasses, or contacts?

A Flexible Spending Account (FSA) is a pre-tax benefit that helps you save on out-of-pocket medical expenses — and that includes vision care. If you’ve been setting money aside each paycheck, your FSA can cover much more than you might think.

blocks.html: Whether you’re overdue for your annual FSA eye exam, or you’ve been eyeing a fresh frame style, now is the moment to use those funds wisely.

blocks.text: 5 Smart Ways to Use Your Remaining FSA Dollars
blocks.html: 5 Smart Ways to Use Your Remaining FSA Dollars
With the deadline approaching, these five ideas offer great value — and peace of mind:

items: [[b]]Schedule your annual eye exam[[/b]][[br]] Vision changes over time. A comprehensive eye exam checks your prescription, monitors eye health, and ensures you’re seeing clearly into the new year.

[[b]]Upgrade your glasses or prescription sunglasses[[/b]][[br]] If your current glasses are outdated, scratched, or no longer suit your style, FSA dollars can cover new frames — or even designer shades with prescription lenses.
[[b]]Order contact lenses or solution[[/b]][[br]] Stock up on your usual lenses or get ahead of supply with extras. Contact lens solution and rewetting drops may also qualify.
[[b]]Treat yourself to blue light protection lenses[[/b]][[br]] Spending hours on screens? Blue light filtering lenses can reduce eye strain and are a smart, FSA-eligible add-on.

[[b]]Stock up on backup eyewear for travel or work[[/b]][[br]] A second pair isn’t a luxury — it’s a lifesaver when your primary pair breaks or gets lost. FSA funds can make that backup plan a reality.
